title: Machine-readable result transport still requires host JSON
observed_need: Expose a stable result document to mncs-actions and future Forge without losing typed native values or structured diagnostics.
current_language_behavior: Native assertions, suite verdicts, retained execution values, process-outcome classification, subprocess-fallback execution adjudication, and the Python family-check path's CheckResult policy projection are MNCS-owned. Python still supervises processes, projects typed values and raw diagnostics, serializes its TestResult/CheckResult JSON, and publishes artifacts; the Rust bootstrap CLI retains its JSON and artifact boundaries.
why_insufficient: The new CheckResult application consumes the shared json_emit integer writer for its compact summary, but the complete cross-repository evidence protocol and canonical JSON encoding are not yet an application-level MNCS surface. Python also reassembles UTF-8-safe chunks where native byte fields are bounded to 1,024 bytes.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py::check_result calls test-check-result-projection for the family check envelope, then serializes the typed native result as mncs.check-result/1 JSON.
desired_direction: A versioned native serialization/protocol library for bounded structured results, with explicit text/bytes policy and lossless adapter projections.
workaround: The MNCS test-check-result-projection application owns CheckResult policy and reference construction. Python reassembles bounded unresolved-message chunks and serializes public JSON/artifacts. Python also retains process supervision, typed-value projection, raw diagnostic transport, and explicit Actions/compatibility transport; it no longer classifies subprocess transport or decoded execution outcomes.
